claim: CMTM5 expression is highly enriched in oligodendrocytes according to bulk RNAseq data.
source: published RNA sequencing data Zhang et al., 2014 demonstrate that mature oligodendrocytes (MOL) display substantial abundance of Cmtm5 mRNA but not of any other gene family member (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2014 and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing RNAseq data

claim: Cmtm5 mRNA is enriched in oligodendrocytes and its abundance increases with differentiation from progenitor to myelinating oligodendrocyte stage.
source: Indeed, Cmtm5 mRNA is enriched in oligodendrocytes, in which its abundance increases with differentiation from the progenitor (OPC) stage to the myelinating oligodendrocytes (MOL) stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing developmental expression data

claim: MOL express CMTM5/Cmtm5 mRNA in both humans and mice according to scRNA-seq data.
source: When evaluating mRNA abundance according to published scRNA-seq data (Jäkel et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2020), MOL (as annotated by high-level expression of myelin basic protein mRNA, MBP/Mbp) express CMTM5/Cmtm5 mRNA in both humans and mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jäkel et al., 2019 and Zhou et al., 2020, and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–F showing scRNA-seq data

claim: Astrocytes display a low level of CMTM5/Cmtm5 mRNA expression.
source: Additional to its expression in oligodendrocytes, astrocytes also display a low level of CMTM5/Cmtm5 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C, E).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C, E showing expression data

claim: CMTM5 protein is detected at the expected molecular weight of 18 kDa by immunoblotting.
source: One band was detected at the expected molecular weight of 18 kDa.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data described in the text and shown in Figure 1A

claim: The abundance of CMTM5 is markedly higher in myelin-enriched fraction than in brain lysates.
source: Indeed, the abundance of CMTM5 was markedly higher in the myelin-enriched fraction than in brain lysates (Figure 1A), similar to the myelin markers PLP, CNP, and SIRT2.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1A comparing myelin and brain lysate

claim: CMTM5 is localized in CNS myelin of C57Bl/6N mice as shown by confocal imaging.
source: Confocal imaging of immunolabeled spinal cord sections revealed CMTM5 in CNS myelin of c57Bl/6N mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1B

claim: CMTM5 labeling is not detected in myelin of conditional Cmtm5 knockout mice (Cmtm5fl/fl;CnpCre/Wt).
source: Importantly, no labeling was found when analyzing corresponding sections of newly generated conditional mouse mutants with a deletion of the Cmtm5 gene in myelinating cells (Cmtm5fl/fl;CnpCre/Wt, also termed cKO; see below) (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1B comparing control and cKO mice

claim: The abundance of CMTM5 in wild-type mouse brains increases coinciding with myelin formation and maturation between postnatal days 15 and 24.
source: By immunoblotting of homogenized wild-type mouse brains, the abundance of CMTM5 increased coinciding with myelin formation and maturation between postnatal days 15 (P15) and 24 (P24) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C showing developmental time course

claim: The abundance of CMTM5 in adult mouse brains remains unchanged between 6 and 24 months of age.
source: In adult mouse brains between 6 and 24 months of age, the abundance of CMTM5 remained unchanged (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C showing aging time course

claim: The abundance of CMTM5 in purified myelin remains essentially constant across ages.
source: The abundance of CMTM5 in purified myelin also remained essentially constant (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1D

claim: CMTM5 is undetectable in myelin purified from brains of Cmtm5 cKO mice by immunoblotting.
source: By immunoblotting, CMTM5 was readily detected in myelin purified from the brains of control mice but undetectable in Cmtm5 cKO myelin (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Cmtm5 cKO mice display a largely similar myelin proteome composition as control mice by label-free quantitative proteome analysis.
source: By label-free quantitative proteome analysis, Cmtm5 cKO mice displayed a largely similar myelin proteome composition as control mice (Figure 2B and B').
evidence: Supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 2B and B'

claim: CMTM5 was undetectable in myelin purified from brains of Cmtm5 cKO mice by mass spectrometry.
source: As an exception, CMTM5 was undetectable in myelin purified from the brains of Cmtm5 cKO mice
evidence: Supported by proteomics data described in text and shown in Figure 2B and B'

claim: The relative abundance of CNP is approximately halved in Cmtm5 cKO myelin due to heterozygosity of the Cnp gene in the CnpCre/Wt driver mice.
source: the relative abundance of CNP was approximately halved as previously shown for the utilized CnpCre/Wt driver mice owing to heterozygosity of the Cnp gene (Erwig et al., 2019; Lappe-Siefke et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by proteomics data and citations to Erwig et al., 2019 and Lappe-Siefke et al., 2003

claim: Cmtm5 cKO mice do not show signs of hypomyelination at P30 and P75.
source: By morphometry, we did not observe signs of hypomyelination (Figure 2D and I )
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy morphometry data shown in Figure 2D and I

claim: Cmtm5 cKO mice do not show myelin pathology such as myelin outfoldings, inner-tongue swellings, or lamella splittings.
source: or myelin pathology such as myelin outfoldings, inner-tongue swellings, or lamella splittings (Figure 2E and J).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 2E and J

claim: The thickness of myelin sheaths (g-ratio) is virtually the same in Cmtm5 cKO and control mice.
source: The thickness of myelin sheaths, as determined by the g-ratio, was also virtually the same in Cmtm5 cKO and control mice (Figure 2F, G, K, L).
evidence: Supported by g-ratio analysis shown in Figure 2F, G, K, L

claim: Cmtm5 cKO mice display an unaltered number of CAII-positive mature oligodendrocytes.
source: By immunohistochemistry, Cmtm5 cKO mice displayed an unaltered number of cells immunopositive for carbonic anhydrase 2 (CAII), a marker for mature oligodendrocytes (Figure 2M and N).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2M and N

claim: MRI shows no apparent differences in brain morphometry and diffusivity in various white and gray matter areas between 8-month-old Cmtm5 cKO and control mice.
source: We then used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess the brains of 8-month-old Cmtm5 cKO and respective control mice. However, no apparent differences in brain morphometry and diffusivity were found in various white and gray matter areas (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by MRI data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: CMTM5 is virtually undetectable in whole-brain lysates of Cmtm5 cKO mice, implying that non-oligodendroglial cells do not contribute substantially to CMTM5 expression in mature brains.
source: CMTM5 was readily detected in whole-brain lysates of control mice but virtually undetectable in Cmtm5 cKO whole-brain lysates (Figure 2O). This implies that non-oligodendroglial cells do not contribute substantially to expression of CMTM5 in mature brains.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 2O and logical inference from the data

claim: Axonal diameters are not altered in optic nerves of Cmtm5 cKO mice.
source: Yet, the quantitative assessment of TEMs did not reveal abnormal axonal diameters in the optic nerves of Cmtm5 cKO mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy morphometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B

claim: Axonal diameters are normal in mice lacking CMTM5 in all cells (Cmtm5-/-) compared to controls.
source: Axonal diameters were also normal in mice lacking CMTM5 in all cells (Cmtm5-/-) compared to respective controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy morphometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: The frequency of pathological-appearing axonal profiles increases over time in optic nerves of Cmtm5 cKO mice compared to controls.
source: When quantifying these profiles at three different ages, we found their frequency to increase over time in the optic nerves of Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy quantification shown in Figure 3A and B across multiple timepoints

claim: Pathological profiles are evident in Cmtm5 cKO optic nerves already at P30.
source: Pathological profiles were evident in Cmtm5 cKO optic nerves already at P30
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy data described in text and shown in Figure 3B

claim: The number of pathological profiles progressively increases toward 12 months of age in Cmtm5 cKO optic nerves.
source: and their number progressively increased toward 12 months of age, the oldest analyzed timepoint.
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy quantification shown in Figure 3B

claim: Axonal density is significantly reduced in Cmtm5 cKO mice at 12 months of age.
source: We observed a trend toward a reduced density of axons in Cmtm5 cKO mice at P30 and P75 that reached significance at 12 months of age (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by axon counting data shown in Figure 3C with statistical significance at 12 months

claim: The observed axonal pathology ultimately leads to axonal loss.
source: This implies that the observed axonal pathology ultimately leads to axonal loss.
evidence: Inferred from the progressive increase in pathological profiles and reduced axonal density

claim: The number of pathological profiles is increased several fold in spinal cord dorsal white matter of Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice at 12 months of age.
source: Indeed, the number of pathological profiles was increased several fold in Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice (Figure 3D and E)
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy quantification shown in Figure 3D and E

claim: The axonopathy observed in Cmtm5 cKO mice is not restricted to the optic nerve.
source: indicating that the observed axonopathy is not restricted to the optic nerve.
evidence: Inferred from finding pathological profiles in both optic nerve and spinal cord

claim: The concentration of myo-inositol is significantly increased in the corpus callosum of Cmtm5 cKO mice compared to controls at 8 months of age.
source: We found the concentrations of myo-inositol significantly increased in the corpus callosi of Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice at 8 months of age (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by magnetic resonance spectroscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A

claim: Cmtm5 cKO brains display a trend toward reduced concentrations of NAA, which did not reach significance.
source: Cmtm5 cKO brains displayed a trend toward reduced concentrations of NAA, which did not reach significance (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by magnetic resonance spectroscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B

claim: At ages P30 and P75, there are no genotype-dependent differences between Cmtm5 cKO and control mice with respect to APP-immunopositive axonal swellings or the relative area of immunopositivity for GFAP, IBA1, or MAC3.

evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A-H

claim: At 12 months of age, all neuropathological markers (APP, GFAP, IBA1, MAC3) are significantly increased in Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice.
source: At 12 months of age, however, all markers were significantly increased in Cmtm5 cKO compared to control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 3I–L).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3I–L

claim: The numbers of myelin outfoldings, inner-tongue inclusions, and axoplasmic inclusions are not increased in Cmtm5 cKO mice at 12 months.
source: We found that the numbers of myelin outfoldings, inner-tongue inclusions, and axoplasmic inclusions are not increased in Cmtm5 cKO mice (Figure 4A''–C'').
evidence: Supported by FIB-SEM quantification shown in Figure 4A''–C''

claim: The number of myelin whorls is markedly increased in Cmtm5 cKO mice at 12 months.
source: Interestingly, however, the number of myelin whorls is markedly increased in Cmtm5 cKO mice (Figure 4D'').
evidence: Supported by FIB-SEM quantification shown in Figure 4D''

claim: Myelin whorls are multilamellar structures that display the periodicity of CNS myelin devoid of a discernible axon, probably best interpreted as remnants of degenerating myelinated fibers with relative sparing of myelin membranes.
source: Myelin whorls are multilamellar structures that largely display the periodicity of CNS myelin devoid of a discernible axon, probably best interpreted as remnants of degenerating myelinated fibers with relative sparing of myelin membranes (Edgar et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Edgar et al., 2009 and knowledge of myelin whorl structure

claim: Axonal degeneration, but not myelin pathology, emerges when oligodendrocytes lack CMTM5.
source: These data indicate that axonal degeneration – but not myelin pathology such as myelin outfoldings or inner-tongue inclusions – emerges when oligodendrocytes lack CMTM5.
evidence: Inferred from FIB-SEM data showing increased myelin whorls but not other myelin pathologies

claim: ERG waveforms, thresholds, and a-wave and b-wave amplitudes do not differ between Cmtm5 cKO and control mice at 8.5 months, indicating normal retinal function.
source: ERG waveforms (Figure 5A), ERG thresholds (Figure 5B), and the amplitudes of the a- and b-waves (Figure 5C and D) did not differ between the genotypes, indicating normal retinal function.
evidence: Supported by ERG data shown in Figure 5A-D

claim: VEPs imply that transmission of signals via the optic nerves to the visual cortex is impaired in Cmtm5 cKO mice.
source: However, visually evoked potentials (VEPs) implied that transmission of signals via the optic nerves to the visual cortex was impaired in Cmtm5 cKO mice (Figure 5E–H).
evidence: Supported by VEP data shown in Figure 5E-H

claim: All mice display sizeable VEPs with normal thresholds and normal VEP latency, indicating normal speed of action potential propagation.
source: All mice displayed sizeable VEPs (Figure 5E) with normal thresholds (Figure 5F) and a normal VEP latency (Figure 5G), indicating normal speed of action potential propagation and probably reflecting normal myelination in the optic nerves.
evidence: Supported by VEP data shown in Figure 5E-G and inference about myelination

claim: VEP amplitudes are significantly reduced in Cmtm5 cKO mice, probably owing to the axonopathy.
source: However, the VEP amplitudes were significantly reduced in Cmtm5 cKO mice (Figure 5H), probably owing to the axonopathy (Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: Supported by VEP data shown in Figure 5H and inference linking to axonopathy data

claim: CMTM5 is undetectable in myelin purified from brains of Cmtm5-/- mice.
source: As expected, CMTM5 was readily detectable by immunoblot in myelin purified from the brains of control mice but undetectable in Cmtm5-/- myelin.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data described in text and shown in Figure 6A

claim: The abundance of CNP appears similar in Cmtm5-/- and Cmtm5Wt/Wt control myelin.
source: Importantly, the abundance of CNP appeared similar in Cmtm5-/- and Cmtm5Wt/Wt control myelin (Figure 6A)

claim: The abundance of PLP and CNP in myelin does not depend on CMTM5 and vice versa the abundance of CMTM5 in myelin does not depend on PLP or CNP.
source: Thus, the abundance of PLP and CNP in myelin does not depend on CMTM5 and vice versa the abundance of CMTM5 in myelin does not depend on PLP or CNP.
evidence: Inferred from immunoblot data showing independent expression levels

claim: Cmtm5-/- mice show a progressive increase in the number of pathological profiles in optic nerves compared to control mice.
source: Notably, by quantitative assessment of electron micrographs we found a progressive increase in the number of pathological profiles in Cmtm5-/- compared to control mice (Figure 6B and C)
evidence: Supported by electron microscopy quantification shown in Figure 6B and C

claim: The axonopathy that emerges when oligodendrocytes lack CMTM5 is independent of Cnp heterozygosity.
source: Importantly, this indicates that the axonopathy that emerges when oligodendrocytes lack CMTM5 is independent of Cnp heterozygosity.

claim: The abundance of CMTM5 is greatly reduced in myelin purified from brains of Cmtm5 iKO mice 4 months after tamoxifen injection.

claim: Cmtm5 iKO mice display a significantly increased number of pathological profiles 4 months after tamoxifen injection.
source: Importantly, by quantitative assessment of electron micrographs, Cmtm5 iKO mice displayed a significantly increased number of pathological profiles 4 months after tamoxifen injection (Figure 6E and F).

claim: Continued oligodendroglial expression of CMTM5 in adult mice is required to prevent the emergence of axonopathy.
source: This indicates that continued oligodendroglial expression of CMTM5 in adult mice is required to prevent the emergence of axonopathy.
evidence: Inferred from finding axonopathy in adult-induced knockout mice

claim: RGC numbers are similar between Cmtm5 cKO and control mice at 12 months of age.

claim: Neuronal cell bodies are preserved in Cmtm5 cKO mice despite axonopathy.
source: indicating that neuronal cell bodies are preserved.

claim: Cmtm5Wt/Wt mice display only a negligible number of pathological profiles, independent of the presence of the WldS mutation.

evidence: Supported by electron microscopy quantification shown in Figure 7E

source: Together, these results imply a Wallerian-type pathomechanism of axonopathy when oligodendrocytes lack Cmtm5.

claim: Oligodendrocytes facilitate rapid impulse propagation along the axons they myelinate and support their long-term integrity.
source: Oligodendrocytes facilitate rapid impulse propagation along the axons they myelinate and support their long-term integrity.
